sources.title: Maestro README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: Cross-platform Electron workspace with parallel agent sessions, Auto Run Markdown checklists or goal loops, remote control, usage views and Git worktree tools. Feature docs may include prerelease behavior.

sources.title: Maestro license
sources.finding: The cited root license governs this repository distribution, subject to component notices.

sources.title: Maestro build manifest
sources.finding: Pinned build metadata identifies the implementation used by the documented application.

sources.title: Maestro Provider notes
sources.finding: Documents CLI transports, credential funding and provider-specific limits, including Standard-mode restrictions over SSH.

sources.title: Maestro Auto Run and Playbooks
sources.locator: Setting up; Tasks; Model Override; Human-in-the-loop
sources.finding: Markdown checklists or goal loops run explicitly; active documents are read-only except paused runs. Per-run model and effort overrides are supported.

sources.title: Maestro SSH remote execution
sources.locator: Overview; Configuring SSH Remotes; Per-Session Configuration; Collaborating over SSH; Limitations
sources.finding: Agents run on user-provided SSH hosts; remote CLI installation and credentials are prerequisites. Optional per-session shared history writes per-hostname JSONL files to the remote project, shown with hostname badges.

sources.title: Maestro Maestro CLI
sources.locator: Sending messages; Global Flags; Auto Run
sources.finding: CLI sends/resumes agent sessions, runs playbooks and exposes structured JSON and failure codes. Some commands require the app reachable.

sources.title: Maestro Group Chat
sources.locator: How it Works; Moderator role; Availability
sources.finding: A moderator coordinates named agents over multiple turns and routes results. Participants do not automatically see each other replies.

sources.title: Maestro Remote control
sources.finding: A browser/phone client uses the full host UI. URL token grants full control; LIVE-off returns loopback-only and rotates the token.

sources.title: Maestro Git and worktrees
sources.locator: Git menu; Worktree agents; Setup scripts
sources.finding: Git log/diff and PR actions integrate with nested worktree agents. Setup scripts run before first agent prompt, on the selected local/SSH host.

sources.title: Maestro Memories
sources.finding: Claude-only project memory viewer reads/edits/deletes Markdown memory; other providers do not expose this panel.

sources.title: Maestro History
sources.finding: Timestamped AUTO/USER/AGENT/CUE entries can be searched and reopened by session ID; immutability is not established.

sources.title: Maestro Configuration
sources.finding: Update check sends UUID/version/platform/theme telemetry, disabled with update checking. Folder sync warns against simultaneous devices and has no conflict resolution.

sources.title: Maestro Agent resilience
sources.locator: Strategies; Never retry; Status card; Quit
sources.finding: Provider overload/quota errors retry with visible cards; credential/permission/crash failures do not. Pending retries do not survive app quit.

sources.title: Maestro README.md
sources.locator: How it works; Features; Quick start
sources.finding: Maestro passes prompts to locally configured provider CLIs and inherits their MCP tools, skills, permissions and authentication. Desktop installation supports user-owned operation. Its documentation MCP server searches docs rather than controlling tasks.

sources.title: Maestro docs/group-chat.md
sources.locator: Agent availability; Message queue; Remote agents
sources.finding: Group Chat moderators coordinate named local/remote agents. By default busy agents wait up to 15 minutes; disabling that safeguard permits concurrent file edits without a lock. Chat queues persist across reload/quit, restart paused, and retain failed sends until manual resume. Group chats can be deleted with their conversation history.

sources.title: Maestro docs/autorun-playbooks.md
sources.locator: Creating Tasks; Running Multiple Auto Run Documents; How a Goal Run Stops; Steering a Run in Flight; Auto-Resume After an Error; Human-in-the-Loop Gates; Stalled Documents; Halt Marker
sources.finding: Goal runs stop on completion, deadlock, finite iteration cap or three stalled iterations. Desktop HITL markers pause until Done, Resume; CLI emits document_gated and skips the document. Three no-progress dispatches abandon a document. Halt markers stop the playbook and prevent replay until removed. Per-run auto-resume defaults to five attempts. Steering notes typed in the Thought Stream are delivered at the start of the next task. Checkboxes and the editor reopen while a run is paused; Reset on Completion keeps working copies in runs/.

sources.title: Maestro docs/history.md
sources.locator: Entry types; Validated flag; Storage; Cross-host history
sources.finding: History links summaries, session IDs, timestamps and output. Validated is only a personal bookmark, not an execution gate. Entries can be deleted. JSON history defaults to 10000 entries per session; cross-host shared history is enabled per session through SSH Remote Execution.

sources.title: Maestro docs/configuration.md
sources.finding: Update-linked anonymous check-ins exclude prompts, agent output, file paths and project names. Disabling startup update checks disables check-ins. Optional cloud-folder sync includes settings/sessions/groups; simultaneous devices can conflict with last write winning and no conflict resolution.

sources.title: Maestro Before you start; Operate; Known limits
sources.locator: Before you start; Operate; Known limits
sources.finding: Cue can run exported pipelines on Linux/systemd or containers without a desktop or logged-in user. Agents use server-side logins and YOLO permissions. Run database stores activity without output; engine logs hold output. In-flight runs become failed after engine restart. Stopping SSH shell steps stops the SSH client, not the remote command.

sources.title: Maestro Overview; Available tools; Technical details
sources.finding: Mintlify-hosted public read-only MCP exposes SearchMaestro for documentation search/retrieval, not session/task control. HTTP transport needs no authentication.

sources.title: Maestro homepage
sources.locator: 'The stage door' section; Legal footer (AGPL-3.0 License link); 'Elsewhere' (maestro-p)
sources.finding: Says Maestro is open source under AGPL-3.0. Downloads come from GitHub Releases, and the page shows no price or pricing page. maestro-p is described as running claude -p on your own Claude Max quota.

sources.title: Maestro docs index
sources.finding: The docs index describes running several accounts of the same provider and spreading work across their plan quotas, so model usage stays on your own provider accounts. No pricing page is listed.

sources.title: Maestro agent ID list
sources.finding: The canonical agent ID list at v1.0.2 includes claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, antigravity, qwen3-coder, opencode, factory-droid, hermes, pi, copilot-cli, omp and grok.

sources.title: Maestro Pi agent definition
sources.finding: The visible Pi definition spawns the pi binary in JSON output mode with session resume, read-only tool restriction and model override.

sources.title: Maestro Grok CLI agent definition
sources.finding: The visible Grok CLI definition spawns the grok binary in batch mode with streaming JSON output and resume; there is no interactive PTY integration.

sources.title: Maestro Gemini CLI agent definition
sources.finding: The gemini-cli definition is marked hidden and commented as not shipping, superseded by Antigravity, and kept only for type compatibility.

sources.title: Maestro README supported agents
sources.finding: README lists the supported coding CLIs and says Gemini CLI support is planned based on user demand, i.e. not currently supported. Line 106 repeats that Gemini CLI may be added in future releases.

sources.title: Maestro provider notes: Pi
sources.finding: Documents Pi provider features (image attachments, session resume, read-only mode, cost tracking, model selection) and that Maestro uses Pi's JSON output mode.

sources.title: Maestro README license
sources.finding: README states the project is under the AGPL-3.0 licence and does not mention any paid tier or price.
